title: App Readiness Passport
description: A small, descriptive, tool-naming fingerprint for cross-comparing many apps at a glance: what an app is, what it is built on, how ready it is for LLM-automated development, and how ready it is for production. Sibling to the vendor-neutral .ai/manifest.yaml (which is the agent-facing CONTRACT); the passport is the human/portfolio-facing SCORECARD. Readers MUST ignore fields they do not recognize.

passport.description: Stable schema id (not a URL, so it can't rot).

passportVersion.description: Semver of THIS schema. Additive within a major; readers ignore unknown fields.

generatedBy.description: Who/what produced it: 'manual', a scanner name, a CI job, etc.

migratedFrom.description: Present when this object was LIFTED from an older stored passportVersion rather than freshly assessed. Migrated ordinal values are floors implied by the old shape, not measurements — re-generate to assess them.

declined.description: Gaps the owner has SEEN and deliberately opted out of ('no error tracking by choice'). Owner intent, applied as a read-time overlay — never a scan output, and never a score change: a decline retires the matching blocker line and re-renders it here as a decision. Keyed by field path so it survives every re-scan.

label.description: Human label for the declined field.

blocker.description: The blocker line this decline retired, kept so the choice stays auditable. PAYLOAD ONLY — never a join key; rewording it must not orphan the decline.

findingId.description: 0.4.0: minted id of the finding this decline stands against (e.g. 'prod.zero-observability'). THE join key, because it survives a rewording. Absent on declines recorded before 0.4.0.

at.description: 0.4.0: YYYY-MM-DD the choice was made, so a reader can age it.

needsReconfirm.description: 0.4.0: the accepted gap has CHANGED since it was accepted (severity rose, the finding's kind changed, or the decision aged out). The blocker then STAYS in blockers[] — an accepted risk about a different repo is not an accepted risk.

reconfirmReason.description: What changed, in the sentence the owner is asked to re-decide on.

slug.description: Stable, sortable key for portfolio tables.

purpose.description: One line on what this app is for.

archetype.description: How the repo is run — selects the readiness lens.

license.description: SPDX id or 'none' (legal blocker) or null if unknown.

criticality.description: How much a failure costs — frames how to read the readiness scores.

stack.description: The tool-NAMING block. Unlike .ai/manifest.yaml this DELIBERATELY names concrete tools — that is the whole point of a first-sight comparison.

persistence.description: Each datastore the app relies on. Empty array = stateless.

required.description: false if the app degrades gracefully without it.

monitoring.description: Named observability vendors/tools. THREE-VALUED since 0.4.0: a vendor name = observed; null = the scan looked and found none; the string 'unknown' = the scan could not look at all (the evidence, e.g. package.json, was outside the snapshot). 'unknown' is a scan-coverage fact and MUST NOT be reported as a real gap in the app's stack. evidence.fields[<path>] carries the rung behind each value.

hosting.description: Named: 'vercel', 'aws-ecs', 'fly', 'self-hosted'; null when none was found; 'unknown' when the scan could not look (three-valued, see monitoring).

integrations.description: Every external service the app talks to. The 'kind' is the comparable axis; 'name' is the vendor.

auth.description: How the app authenticates to it: 'oauth', 'api-key', 'iam', 'webhook-secret', ...

secretsFrom.description: Where secrets legitimately come from (vault/keyring/env), never the secrets themselves.

automationReadiness.description: Readiness for FULL LLM-automated development: can an agent understand the repo, act in it, and verify its own change before a human looks? Reuses Ascent's L1..L5 ladder.

level.description: L1 Manual, L2 Assisted, L3 Augmented, L4 Integrated, L5 Autonomous.

artifacts.description: The agent-facing inputs an autonomous agent needs to be effective.

contextGraph.description: Machine-readable map of modules->features (context-map.json, CONTEXT.md coverage).

memory.description: Agent-written memory (decisions, gotchas), GRADED (0.2.0; was boolean in 0.1.0). none = absent · adhoc = present but unstructured (a single flat file / one lone entry) · curated = >=2 structured per-fact entries under .ai|.claude/memory, or an index plus entries · governed = curated PLUS observable process (supersede/replaces links between entries, a schema/policy file, or a CI job that checks the memory tree).

manifest.description: Carries an agent-facing capability manifest (.ai/manifest.yaml or equivalent).

evals.description: Golden/eval tests for any LLM-produced output.

skills.description: Reusable agent skills / subagents, GRADED (0.2.0; was boolean in 0.1.0). none = absent · adhoc = present but not a library (loose files, or a single skill) · curated = >=2 distinct skills that each carry their own definition file · governed = curated PLUS observable process (a registry/index at the skills root, a CI job referencing the skills tree, or a package script that lints/validates them).

selfVerify.description: Which capabilities an agent can run LOCALLY to prove a change before push. The more true, the safer autonomy.

aiInWorkflow.description: Evidence AI is actually used (AI co-author trailers, agent-authored PRs), not just configured.

blockers.description: What caps the level — the highest-leverage things to fix next. RENDERED TEXT: a projection of findings[].text, kept for pre-0.4.0 readers.

productionReadiness.description: Readiness to be TRUSTED in production. Each component is an ordinal enum so a portfolio sorts trivially; 'score' and 'band' are the headline.

level.description: none -> build-only -> runs checks (non-blocking) -> checks GATE merge -> automated deploy -> progressive/canary+reversible.
none -> a few -> meaningful but gaps -> critical paths covered -> broad unit+integration+e2e with coverage tracked.

coveragePct.description: Measured line/branch coverage, or null if not tracked.

level.description: none -> SECURITY.md only -> secret/dep scanning present -> SAST/SCA GATES merges -> + SBOM/signing/provenance.
none -> structured logs -> error tracking -> + metrics/dashboards -> + distributed tracing/alerting.

rollback.description: A defined, tested way back (versioned deploys, feature flags).

blockers.description: Release-gating issues, highest severity first. RENDERED TEXT: a projection of findings[].text, kept for pre-0.4.0 readers.

links.description: Pointers to richer artifacts so the passport stays thin.

report.description: Latest full maturity/readiness report this was summarized from.

evidence.description: Provenance, so a reader knows how much to trust the scores.

confidence.description: 0..1 — how much of the app could be inspected.

files.description: Files the assessment was synthesized from — drift-check these.

notes.description: Caveats a reader must carry, e.g. the note a version migration leaves when an ordinal was lifted from an older shape instead of assessed.

fields.description: 0.4.0: PER-FIELD detection strength, keyed by dotted passport path (the same vocabulary the declined[] paths use). Without it a vendor guessed from a dependency list and one read off a fetched command carry identical apparent authority. Deliberately NOT exhaustive — only the named/heuristic fields are rated, so the passport stays one screen long. A reader filtering on strength MUST prefer fields[path] and fall back to evidence.confidence only when the path is absent.

confidence.description: The rung's FIXED value — not a judgement call, so two passports are comparable.

basis.description: observed (1.0) the artifact itself was read; declared (0.8) a dependency/config declaration names it but nothing shows it running; inferred (0.5) a path/name heuristic over the tree index; unobserved (0) the evidence was not in the snapshot and the field reads 'unknown'.

findings.description: 0.4.0: the blockers WITH MINTED IDENTITY. A persisted judgment (an owner decline, a fleet rollup bucket) must attach to a stable id with the rendered string as payload — joining on the prose orphans every decline the moment the wording is regenerated, and splits one rollup bucket into two.

id.description: Axis-scoped CAUSE code, e.g. 'prod.zero-observability'. Stable across rewordings; never derived from the text.

code.description: The cause code without its axis prefix — the fleet rollup bucket key.

text.description: The rendered sentence as of this generation. Payload, never a join key.

severity.description: Ordinal. 'critical' is never emitted by a scan: it is the escalated reading of a 'block' once an owner marks the repo business/mission-critical or GA — the change of circumstance that re-opens an old decline.
